subject: Apply or ddply solution for comparing columns

messages.author: 4dee24c578d7691c
messages.subject: Apply or ddply solution for comparing columns
parts:
Hello dear Davis R users,

I am unfortunately rather stumped on what seems to be a simple problem.

I want to compare the attached data ("SampleData") by each column of
species information (Sp1,2 & 3), to a column of mean information -
"CompValue" by "Site", to generate a dataframe which says whether the
species has "Higher" or "Lower" values than the means.

I thought I could do this by using apply by columns and an ifelse
statement, but I seem to be setting that up wrong somehow, and perhaps I
need another argument in the apply function to indicate that the value
for each column needs to be compared to the corresponding site
comparison value (across rows). I have tried ddply and by and it seems
that I am missing something about how to logically set this up.

Any help much appreciated. The attached files are Sample Data and Sample
Result to get an idea of what I have and where I want to go.

Thanks!,
Stella

--
Stella Copeland
Post-doctoral Researcher
Harrison Lab, Plant Ecology
UC Davis

parts:
Something like:

x <- read.csv(SampleData.csv)

x$comp <- NA

fun <- function(x, comp){
  out <- rep(NA, 1:length(x))
   i <- which(x > comp)
  out[i] <- "gt"
   i <- which(x < comp)
   out[i] <- "lt"

   out
}

result <- apply(x,2, FUN=fun, comp=x$comp)

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Apply or ddply solution for comparing columns
parts:
Hi Stella,

Does this do the trick? You seemed to be on the right path with ifelse.

-Patrick

# the data
test <- data.frame(Site = 1:6,
                   Sp1 = c(25,30,NA, 62, 10, 5),
                   Sp2 = c(15, 3, 4, 2, 1, 0.1),
                   Sp3 = c(3,3,3,NA,4,90),
                   CompValue = c(15,10,2,5,6,4))

# make output dataframe, dropping the CompValue field.
out <- test[,-5]

# use ifelse to compare the values of Sp1, Sp2, and Sp3 columns to CompValue
# and repl
out <- ifelse(out[,c(2,3,4)] > test[,5], "high", "low")
out

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Apply or ddply solution for comparing columns
parts:
Here’s a dplyr implementation:

library(dplyr)

SampleData = structure(list(Site = 1:6, Sp1 = c(25L, 30L, NA, 62L, 10L, 5L
), Sp2 = c(15, 3, 4, 2, 1, 0.1), Sp3 = c(3L, 3L, 3L, NA, 4L, 
90L), CompValue = c(15L, 10L, 2L, 5L, 6L, 4L)), .Names = c("Site", 
"Sp1", "Sp2", "Sp3", "CompValue"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, 
-6L))

SampleResult = SampleData %>%
    mutate_each(funs(ifelse( . > CompValue, "High", "Low")), starts_with("Sp")) %>%
        select(-CompValue)

SampleResult

  Site  Sp1  Sp2  Sp3 CompValue
1    1 High  Low  Low        15
2    2 High  Low  Low        10
3    3 <NA> High High         2
4    4 High  Low <NA>         5
5    5 High  Low  Low         6
6    6 High  Low High         4

mutate_each takes SampleData and modifies any column selected with the last argument (starts_with("Sp")) using the function defined inside funs, where . stands for the input. The last line drops CompValue.

​

Noam
